stories.title: The Birthmonth Of Mr Sadness
stories.description: Nobody knows when or where Mr. Sadness was born, but one year ago he found his way to the invisible Mushroom House and quietly became part of its family. He is a shy, gentle creature who rarely asks for anything, yet whenever Mei opens the door for afternoon tea, he appears with his small smile and settles among the others. Sometimes he gathers nuts from the forest as gifts; sometimes he washes the cups, arranges the kettle, or tends the stove, offering whatever kindness his little hands can manage. Because no one knows his real birthday, the Mushroom House decides to celebrate the entire month in which he first found his home. There will be tea, warm bread, little presents, and plenty of ordinary afternoons together, without requiring Mr. Sadness to become any louder or happier than he wishes. His birthmonth is a celebration not of sadness disappearing, but of a quiet being finding a place where he is loved exactly as he is.

stories.title: The Mushroom Village Beneath The Full Moon
stories.description: On a full-moon night at the end of autumn, the forest grows colder, and the little mushroom villages hidden among its trees begin disappearing one by one beneath an ocean of fallen leaves. In one village, every mushroom is a musician, and each plays a different instrument: cello, violin, piano, or another small voice in their woodland orchestra. They know that their village, too, will soon vanish beneath the leaves, but nobody puts away an instrument or abandons the music. Instead, they continue playing together, their melodies rising through the cold air as the moon illuminates the last roofs and pathways. Gradually, the golden-brown leaves surround the houses, cover the little streets, and swallow the village, while the musicians continue their gentle, living conversation. Their music is neither a protest against disappearing nor a surrender to sadness, but a joyful expression of having been alive together, continuing until the forest becomes quiet.
